entries.appliesTo: operators of AI companion chatbots made available to users in Georgia

dutySources.disclosure-ui: § 39-5-6(b)(1) — 'An operator shall clearly and conspicuously disclose to a user that he or she is interacting with an AI companion chatbot as opposed to a natural person'
dutySources.content-safeguards: § 39-5-6(d) — 'the operator shall institute reasonable measures to prevent the AI companion chatbot from: (1) Producing visual material of sexually explicit conduct'
dutySources.crisis-protocol: § 39-5-6(f) — 'An operator shall not make available an AI companion chatbot unless the operator implements and maintains a protocol for detecting and addressing severe harm or related emotional crises.'
dutySources.age-assurance: § 39-5-6(j) — 'Before allowing access to a feature or mode that may generate synthetic content containing sexually explicit conduct, an operator shall use a commercially reasonable age assurance method proportionate to the risk of the feature.'

sources.scope: § 39-5-6(a)(1)(A) — ''AI companion chatbot' means a system using artificial intelligence, generative artificial intelligence, or emotional recognition algorithms designed to simulate a sustained human or human-like relationship with a user'
sources.ageFocus: § 39-5-6(b)(1) — 'An operator shall clearly and conspicuously disclose to a user' (baseline duties bind as to all users; subsections (c)-(e), (i) and the hourly disclosure apply to minors)
sources.aiDisclosure: § 39-5-6(b)(1)(A) — 'At the beginning of each interaction or session'
sources.crisisProtocol: § 39-5-6(f) — 'implements and maintains a protocol for detecting and addressing severe harm or related emotional crises'
sources.parentalTools: § 39-5-6(i) — 'For accounts known to belong to minor users, an operator shall offer reasonable tools to a minor or parent to manage the minor's screen time and account settings'
sources.engagementLimits: § 39-5-6(e) — 'An operator shall adopt reasonable measures to prevent an AI companion chatbot to use the following techniques directed to a minor … (5) Variable or unpredictable rewards intended to increase engagement.'
sources.contentSafeguards: § 39-5-6(d) — 'institute reasonable measures to prevent the AI companion chatbot from: (1) Producing visual material of sexually explicit conduct; … (5) Role-playing adult-minor romantic relationships'
sources.ageThreshold: § 39-5-6(a)(4) — ''Minor' means an individual who is less than 18 years of age.'
sources.penaltyMax: § 39-5-6(k)(1)(A) — 'A civil penalty of up to $10,000.00 per knowing violation of this Code section'
sources.penaltyUnit: § 39-5-6(k)(1)(A) — 'per knowing violation of this Code section'
sources.enforcer: § 39-5-6(k)(1) — 'The Attorney General may bring a civil action against any operator violating this Code section'
sources.cureDays: § 39-5-6(k)(3) — 'provide written notice and an opportunity to cure within 30 days for a first-time violation'

flags: aiDisclosure lossy: (b)(1) requires disclosure both at session start and 'At least every three hours during continued interaction'; (b)(2) tightens the periodic cadence to 'every hour' for known-minor users or chatbots directed/marketed to minors

ageFocus lossy: disclosure (b)(1), crisis protocol (f), public disclosure (g), licensure-representation ban (h), and age assurance (j) bind as to all users, while (c), (d), (e), (i) and hourly disclosure are minor-specific

(g) requires public website/in-app disclosure of a plain-language crisis-protocol summary and, annually, 'the aggregate number of crisis referral notifications issued in the preceding calendar year' — no matching duty key (public reporting, not incident-reporting to an authority)

(h) prohibits knowingly programming the chatbot to represent 'that it is licensed, certified, or otherwise authorized to provide professional mental health, behavioral health, medical, or counseling services' unless lawfully authorized — no matching duty key

(j) imposes age-assurance data handling limits: no sale of age-assurance data, use limited to age verification, retention capped — 'in no event shall such data be retained longer than 24 hours or another specified time if permitted by law, whichever is longer'

cureDays is discretionary, not mandatory: (k)(3) 'The Attorney General may, in the Attorney General's discretion, provide written notice and an opportunity to cure within 30 days for a first-time violation that does not involve knowing misconduct, sexual exploitation of a minor, or self-harm related misconduct'
penalty multiplier: (k)(2) 'each day in violation of this Code section shall be considered a separate violation for each user affected'
(m)(5) carve-out: no 'liability for the developer of a conversational AI service which is made available to the public by a separate operator'
